issues.title: Setext TOC headings do not honor explicit {#id} anchors
issues.evidence: Commit 8650864 started collecting setext level-2 headings for generated TOCs, but the setext path calls collectTOCHeading with an empty explicit id and never applies headingIDRE. ATX headings strip {#id} before rendering and pass the parsed id; setext headings keep {#custom} in the visible heading text and derive an automatic id from it.
issues.reproduction:
In a temporary HEAD worktree, a scratch test calling RenderMarkdownXHTMLDocument("Custom Section {#custom} -------------------------- Text. ", nil, true) produced html `

Custom Section {#custom}

` and TOC href `#custom-section-custom`; expected `

Custom Section

` and TOC href `#custom`.
issues.notes: README originally said explicit {#id} overrides only on ATX headings, but the feature change made setext headings participate in the same generated TOC surface.

resolution.summary: Setext headings now parse explicit {#id} anchors before rendering and TOC collection, matching ATX behavior; README wording now says ATX or setext.

issues.title: Signed builds mutate output after SignHTML by writing gzip siblings
issues.evidence: In the signed branch, BuildSite calls SignHTML and then calls writeGzipSibling on the final signed path. That creates or replaces a .html.gz file after the attest/attested-html signing step has completed, violating the repository instruction that files must not be mutated after signing and that signing must call attest/attested-html as the final step.
issues.reproduction: Run a signed build, for example the existing TestSignedBuildGzipsTheSignedBytes path with a fake signer. The code signs public/index.html first, then writes public/index.html.gz afterward.
issues.notes: The gzip bytes decompress to the signed HTML, but the build still performs filesystem mutation after signing. User selected keeping signed gzip behavior despite the signing-final-step conflict.

resolution.summary: Runtime behavior intentionally unchanged. No GitHub issue was created; relay text should be handed to the user for external discussion.

issues.title: CSS behavior-property check allows legacy-prefixed behavior declarations
issues.evidence: Commit 690a9da narrowed behavior detection to the regex `(?:^|[{;\s])behavior\s*:` so safe properties like scroll-behavior are allowed. That regex does not match legacy-prefixed declarations such as `*behavior:` or `_behavior:`, even though the code comment says it is blocking the legacy IE behavior HTC property.
issues.reproduction: In a temporary HEAD worktree, a scratch test asserting ValidateCSS(`*behavior: default;`) and ValidateCSS(`_behavior: default;`) should fail instead observed ValidateCSS accepting `*behavior: default;`.
issues.notes: Modern browsers ignore these legacy CSS hacks, but this validator explicitly targets the legacy IE behavior property.

resolution.summary: CSS validation now rejects *behavior: and _behavior: declarations while preserving scroll-behavior and overscroll-behavior.
